ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Persistent dry cough with runny nose; no specific trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Onset 5–6 days ago; cough continuous day and night, causing sleep disturbance; runny nose since onset; chills and myalgias early in course; diarrhea on first day only.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: Mild irritation secondary to coughing; no dysphagia, odynophagia, throat-closing sensation, or voice change.  
  • Nasal: Rhinorrhea present.  
  • Otologic: No ear pain, blockage, or discharge.  
  • Airway/respiratory: No stridor, noisy breathing, or baseline dyspnea; transient sensation of breathlessness only during coughing bouts.  
  • No facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, drooling, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None reported; has not sought emergency care; no prior epinephrine or steroid use.
- Allergies: Denies medication allergies.
- Current medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context: Lives with partner (well); working as IT developer; took one sick day but has been working; ex-smoker (quit 6 months ago); drinks wine 2–3 glasses on up to 3 evenings/week.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not visualized (telephone consultation).
- Airway/breathing: Patient denies labored breathing at rest; no audible stridor reported.
- Mental status: Alert; reports lethargy but no confusion or syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Third-party presence: None during call.

Assessment:
- Probable uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection with persistent dry cough and rhinorrhea; no red-flag ENT airway features at present.

Plan:
- Symptomatic care: Rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol (acetaminophen) as needed.
- Work advice: Take additional 1–2 days off for recovery; reassess ability to return early next week.
- Escalation/red-flag advice: Seek medical review sooner if cough or fever persists >2–3 more days, breathing becomes difficult, or any new symptoms such as chest pain, voice change, throat tightening, stridor, or swelling of face/lips/tongue develop.
- Follow-up: Telephone or in-person review in 2–3 days if no improvement; consider chest exam and possible antibiotics if bacterial infection suspected at that time.
- Lifestyle counsel (secondary to comorbidities): Reduce alcohol intake to ≤2 glasses/week initially; continue smoking abstinence.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs, oxygen saturation, or physical airway exam documented; no explicit review of vaccination status or availability of rescue inhaler/auto-injector (not expected but noted).  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor background pauses but clinically adequate.
